message.content:
You are building three small verification scripts for a Ramp deployment pipeline in the repo at /home/user/Genera. Work only in that repo.

# YOU OWN EXACTLY THESE THREE FILES — create no others, edit no others
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/check_quotes.py
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/check_coverage.py
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/lint_roster.py

Other agents are concurrently writing run_pipeline.py and the references/*.md files. Do NOT touch those, do NOT touch capabilities.yaml, gen_ledger.py, SKILL.md, or anything under candidate/. Do not git commit or push.

# CONTEXT

The pipeline ingests one "customer packet" (raw transcripts, rosters, Slack exports) and emits two JSON files that must validate against shipped schemas. An audit log is half the deliverable: it records assumptions, missing info, conflicts, and things the Ramp API cannot do.

Read these first to ground yourself:
- /home/user/Genera/README.md
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/references/capabilities.yaml  (the capability ledger, 42 rows — SOURCE OF TRUTH)
- /home/user/Genera/candidate/schemas/audit_log_schema.json
- /home/user/Genera/candidate/schemas/ramp_config_schema.json
- /home/user/Genera/candidate/customer_packets/client_a_acme_corp/  (a real packet; the roster CSV there is your lint_roster test case)

# DATA CONTRACTS (fixed — build to these exactly)

Ledger row fields in capabilities.yaml under top-level key `capabilities`:
  id, verdict (one of SUPPORTED|PARTIAL|UI_ONLY|UNSUPPORTED|DRIFT), title,
  customer_phrasings[], api_mechanism{endpoints[],fields[]},
  evidence[{source,checked_on,note}], evidence_line, config_expression{section,mechanism,note}, workaround, seen_in[]

work/<packet>/requirements.json:
{"packet": "client_a_acme_corp",
 "requirements": [
   {"req_id":"REQ-001","claim":"CEO card should effectively have no limit",
    "source_file":"discovery_call_01.txt",
    "source_quote":"I never want to see a decline",
    "archetype_id":"CAP-UNLIMITED","confidence":"high"}]}
 - source_quote is verbatim text captured at extraction time
 - archetype_id is a ledger row id, or null if nothing matched

work/<packet>/traceability.json:
{"packet": "client_a_acme_corp",
 "entries": [
   {"req_id":"REQ-001","archetype_id":"CAP-UNLIMITED","disposition":"both",
    "config_paths":["limits[3]"],"audit_refs":["assumptions_made[2]"]}]}
 - disposition is "config" | "audit" | "both"
 - config_paths are dotted/indexed paths into ramp_config.json
 - audit_refs are indexed paths into audit_log.json, e.g. "unsupported_api_requests[0]"

out/<packet>/ramp_config.json and out/<packet>/audit_log.json — only these two files in out/.

Packet source files live at candidate/customer_packets/<packet>/<source_file>.

# THE SCRIPTS

## 1. check_quotes.py
CLI: `python3 check_quotes.py --packet <packet_name>` (packet_name is the directory name, e.g. client_a_acme_corp)
Purpose: catch hallucinated citations. For every requirement in requirements.json, assert source_quote appears VERBATIM in candidate/customer_packets/<packet>/<source_file>.
- Normalize whitespace (collapse runs of whitespace to single spaces) on both sides before comparing, and normalize unicode quotes/dashes to ASCII equivalents — transcripts use curly quotes and em dashes, and an extractor may normalize them. Do NOT lowercase.
- Fail if source_file does not exist in the packet.
- On failure print the req_id, the source_file, and the first ~70 chars of the offending quote.
- Exit 0 if all quotes verify, 1 otherwise. Print a one-line summary either way ("N/N quotes verified").
Target ~45 lines.

## 2. check_coverage.py
CLI: `python3 check_coverage.py --packet <packet_name>`
Reads work/<packet>/requirements.json, work/<packet>/traceability.json, out/<packet>/audit_log.json, and the ledger.
Runs four checks, each a small named function, and reports ALL failures (do not stop at the first). Exit 1 if any fail.

  (a) COVERAGE INVARIANT — every req_id in requirements.json must have a traceability entry with at least one config_path or audit_ref. Orphans fail the run. Also fail on a traceability entry whose req_id is not in requirements.json.

  (b) FALSE-POSITIVE SWEEP — for every traceability entry whose audit_refs include an "unsupported_api_requests[...]" ref, look up its archetype_id in the ledger. If that row's verdict is SUPPORTED, FAIL. Rationale: claiming the API cannot do something it demonstrably can is explicitly graded. Entries with archetype_id null are skipped with a warning line (not a failure).

  (c) FALSE-NEGATIVE SWEEP — for every traceability entry that has config_paths but NO audit_refs, look up its archetype_id. If the verdict is UNSUPPORTED, UI_ONLY, or PARTIAL, FAIL: it has been silently configured as if fully supported, with nothing in the audit log. Verdicts SUPPORTED and DRIFT pass. archetype_id null → warning, not failure.

  (d) EVIDENCE COMPLETENESS — every entry in audit_log.json's unsupported_api_requests[] must have a non-empty `evidence` string containing a 4-digit year (a date), so evidence is always dated. Report the index of any that fail.

Print a compact pass/fail line per check plus details for failures, naming req_ids. This script may run to ~90 lines since it bundles four checks; keep each check its own function.

## 3. lint_roster.py
CLI: `python3 lint_roster.py <path-to-csv> [--json]`
Purpose: deterministic detection of roster dirt an LLM skims past. Produces findings that become conflicts/missing-info rows.
Detect, using heuristic column matching (case-insensitive substring on headers, so it works on unseen packets):
  - duplicate rows by email (report each email and the differing values across its rows — the point is to surface the disagreement, e.g. two different limits)
  - blank/empty cells in any detected limit column, and blank emails
  - non-numeric values in a limit column (e.g. "NO LIMIT")
  - case-variant / whitespace-variant values within a department-like column (e.g. "sales" vs "Sales") that would create duplicate departments
  - dangling manager references: a manager-email column value that is not itself an email in the roster (blank manager is fine — that is the top of the chain)
Column detection: find the header containing "email" (and not "manager") for identity; "manager" for manager refs; "depart" for department; "limit" for limits. If a column is absent, skip that check rather than crashing.
Output: human-readable summary by default; with --json emit a JSON object {"findings":[{"kind":...,"detail":...,"rows":[...]}]} to stdout.
Exit 0 ALWAYS (this is a reporting tool, not a gate) — but print a clear count of findings.
Target ~60 lines.

Verify it against candidate/customer_packets/client_a_acme_corp/department_roster.csv, which genuinely contains: a duplicated email with two different limits, a blank limit, a "NO LIMIT" string, lowercase "sales" alongside "Sales", and a manager email that appears nowhere as a roster member. Your script MUST find all five classes there. Report in your final message exactly what it found.

# GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
- Python 3, standard library only EXCEPT `yaml` (pyyaml is installed) for reading the ledger.
- Each script: a module docstring explaining what it catches and why that matters, and a `main()` returning an exit code, invoked via `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`.
- Resolve repo paths relative to the script's own location (the scripts live at .claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/, so the repo root is three parents up) — never rely on the caller's cwd.
- Make paths overridable with an optional `--repo` argument defaulting to that computed root.
- Legibility matters more than cleverness: a reviewer should understand each script in about a minute.
- Match the house style of the existing /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/gen_ledger.py — read it first and follow its conventions (docstring, constants, small functions, argparse-free simple sys.argv handling is fine if that is what it does).

# TESTING (required — do not skip)
You have no requirements.json or traceability.json to test against. CREATE TEMPORARY FIXTURES under /tmp to test check_quotes.py and check_coverage.py: build a small requirements.json/traceability.json/audit_log.json that exercises both the passing and the failing path of every check (including a deliberate false-positive and a deliberate false-negative), run the scripts with --repo pointed at your fixture tree, and confirm they pass and fail as intended. Do NOT leave fixtures inside /home/user/Genera — put them in /tmp. Delete nothing from the repo.

In your final message report: each script's line count, exactly what lint_roster.py found in the real packet A roster, and the results of your fixture tests for both the pass and fail paths of checks (a)-(d).

# Genera Take-Home — Ramp Deployment Pipeline

Turns one customer packet (raw transcripts, rosters, Slack exports, policy memos) into
two JSON files: a desired-state `ramp_config.json` and an `audit_log.json` that says
what was assumed, what is missing, what conflicts, and what Ramp cannot actually do.

The exercise spec is `candidate/README.md` and it is the source of truth for direction.

## Layout

```
.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/
  references/
    capabilities.yaml       SOURCE OF TRUTH — the capability ledger
    CAPABILITY_LEDGER.md    generated from the yaml, committed so it reads without running
  scripts/
    gen_ledger.py           regenerates the markdown; --check fails on staleness
candidate/                  exercise material, committed so the repo stays runnable
work/                       intermediates (requirements.json) — not graded
out/                        ONLY the two graded JSONs per packet
session/                    session export
```

## The capability ledger

The ledger is the part that makes this reusable. Its unit is *a thing customers ask for*
("the card must decline for this vendor"), not an endpoint — so a row written for one
packet answers the same question in the next one, including packets nobody has seen.

Each row carries a verdict (SUPPORTED / PARTIAL / UI_ONLY / UNSUPPORTED / DRIFT), the
endpoints and fields that implement it, dated evidence, and — for anything not fully
supported — a workaround. `evidence_line` is copied verbatim into audit-log evidence
fields, which is how several audit logs stay consistent with each other instead of each
re-arguing the same point.

Regenerate and check the markdown:

```
python3 .claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/gen_ledger.py
python3 .claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/gen_ledger.py --check
```

## Validating outputs

```
python3 candidate/tools/validate.py out/<packet>/ramp_config.json out/<packet>/audit_log.json
```

# Ramp capability ledger — SOURCE OF TRUTH.
#
# The unit is *a thing customers ask for*, not an endpoint. That is what makes a row
# reusable across packets (including packets nobody has seen yet).
#
# CAPABILITY_LEDGER.md is GENERATED from this file by scripts/gen_ledger.py.
# Edit this file, never the markdown.
#
# verdict:
#   SUPPORTED   — the Developer API can express it directly.
#   PARTIAL     — expressible, but with a material caveat (fan-out, granularity loss, scope).
#   UI_ONLY     — real Ramp capability, but configured in-app; no Developer API write surface.
#   UNSUPPORTED — the product does not do this, by API or UI, as far as evidence shows.
#   DRIFT       — a discrepancy between schemas/ as shipped and the live API. Log, do not fix.
#
# evidence[].source values:
#   openapi_snapshot_2026_08_30 — candidate/2026_08_30_Ramp_OpenAPI_Schema.json (primary)
#   docs.ramp.com / support.ramp.com — live docs, with the page and date checked
#
# evidence_line is copied VERBATIM into audit_log evidence fields. That is how five
# audit logs stay consistent with each other instead of each re-arguing the point.

    verdict: UI_ONLY
    title: Multi-tier spend approval chain (threshold -> approver)
    customer_phrasings:

      - "all travel needs my direct approval"
      - "anything over $2,500 escalates"
    api_mechanism:
      endpoints: []
      fields: []
    evidence:
      - source: openapi_snapshot_2026_08_30
        checked_on: 2026-08-30
        note: >-
          No approval-policy write endpoint. The only approval paths are
          /developer/v1/blank-canvas-approvals/* (which act on already-existing approval
          trigger instances) and GET /developer/v1/spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes
          (read-only). No approval-related OAuth scope is defined among the 76 scopes.
      - source: support.ramp.com
        checked_on: 2026-08-30
        note: >-
          PASS 2 CORRECTION to the verdict, not the mechanism. Ramp does support multi-tier
          approval chains — in the app. "Set up your spend approval policies" and "Setting up
          spend request approvals" describe an approvals workflow builder where conditions and
          outcomes (Require approval / Notify / Approve spend) are layered and nested, with
          amount and user-role routing available to all customers and further conditions on
          Ramp Plus. So the capability is real and the API cannot reach it. UI_ONLY, not
          UNSUPPORTED — and the "hand it to the deployment owner" workaround is now evidenced
          rather than assumed.
    evidence_line: "openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — no approval-policy write endpoint; only /blank-canvas-approvals/* (acts on existing instances) and GET /spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes (read-only); zero approval OAuth scopes. support.ramp.com 'Set up your spend approval policies', checked 2026-08-30 — tiered approval chains ARE configurable in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder, so this is a UI-only capability rather than a missing one."
    config_expression:

        Still emitted as desired state. The schema's approval_policies description
        explicitly invites this ("check API support"), so the config carries the customer's
        intent and the audit log carries the fact that it cannot be applied via API.
    workaround: >-
      Emit the full tier structure as desired state, then hand the deployment owner a
      UI checklist to build the same chain in Ramp's approvals workflow builder.

    verdict: UNSUPPORTED
    title: Approval triggered by vendor novelty rather than amount

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify every requirement's source_quote really appears in the file it cites.

Catches hallucinated citations: a requirement whose source_quote was paraphrased,
stitched together from two turns, or attributed to the wrong file. Every downstream
audit-log `source` field leans on these quotes, so an unverified quote is a lie the
whole deliverable inherits.

  python3 check_quotes.py --packet client_a_acme_corp [--repo /path/to/repo]

Exit 0 if every quote verifies, 1 otherwise.
"""
import sys, json, pathlib, unicodedata

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
# Transcripts use curly quotes and em dashes; an extractor may have normalized them.
FOLD = {"‘": "'", "’": "'", "‚": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"',
        "„": '"', "–": "-", "—": "-", "−": "-", "…": "..."}


def norm(text):
    """Fold unicode punctuation to ASCII and collapse whitespace. Case is preserved."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text)
    return " ".join("".join(FOLD.get(ch, ch) for ch in text).split())


def arg(flag, default=None):
    return sys.argv[sys.argv.index(flag) + 1] if flag in sys.argv else default


def main():
    root = pathlib.Path(arg("--repo", ROOT))
    packet = arg("--packet")
    if not packet:
        print("usage: check_quotes.py --packet <packet_name> [--repo <path>]")
        return 1

    reqs = json.loads((root / "work" / packet / "requirements.json").read_text())["requirements"]
    packet_dir = root / "candidate" / "customer_packets" / packet
    cache, bad = {}, []

    for r in reqs:
        src = packet_dir / r["source_file"]
        if src.name not in cache:
            cache[src.name] = norm(src.read_text()) if src.is_file() else None
        haystack = cache[src.name]
        if haystack is None:
            bad.append((r["req_id"], r["source_file"], "MISSING FILE", r.get("source_quote", "")))
        elif norm(r["source_quote"]) not in haystack:
            bad.append((r["req_id"], r["source_file"], "QUOTE NOT FOUND", r["source_quote"]))

    for req_id, src_file, why, quote in bad:
        print(f"FAIL {req_id}  {why}  in {src_file}\n     quote: {norm(quote)[:70]!r}")
    print(f"{len(reqs) - len(bad)}/{len(reqs)} quotes verified")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
PYEOF
